description: Table 4 is a stand-alone rendered data table (no axes, spectra or micrographs) presented as "Experimental verification of model prediction results". It has five columns with the exact headers "YS/MPa", "Extra trees predicted value /MPa", "Difference /MPa", "GA-Extra Trees predicted values/ MPa" and "Difference /MPa", and three data rows. The measured yield strengths (YS) are 709, 968 and 964 MPa; the Extra trees predictions are 743, 999 and 928 MPa, giving absolute differences of 34, 31 and 36 MPa; after genetic-algorithm (GA) feature selection/optimisation the GA-Extra Trees predictions are 721, 978 and 945 MPa, with differences of 12, 10 and 19 MPa. The table therefore demonstrates that in every one of the three cases the GA-Extra Trees error is smaller than the plain Extra trees error, the reduction being 22, 21 and 17 MPa respectively. No temperature, alloy or condition label is printed anywhere in the table itself; the citing text maps the three rows to 750 °C, 800 °C and 850 °C. Because both model deviations are tabulated row-by-row against the measured YS, this table is the quantitative backing for the claim that GA-optimised Extra Trees improves YS prediction for medium-manganese low-density steel.

observations.observation: The table has five columns with the printed headers 'YS/MPa', 'Extra trees predicted value /MPa', 'Difference /MPa', 'GA-Extra Trees predicted values/ MPa' and 'Difference /MPa'.
Three measured yield strengths are listed in the first column: 709, 968 and 964 MPa.
The Extra trees predictions are 743, 999 and 928 MPa, with printed absolute differences of 34, 31 and 36 MPa.
The GA-Extra Trees predictions are 721, 978 and 945 MPa, with printed absolute differences of 12, 10 and 19 MPa.
For all three rows the GA-Extra Trees difference is smaller than the Extra trees difference (12<34, 10<31, 19<36 MPa).
The reduction in prediction error achieved by GA optimisation is 22 MPa (row 1), 21 MPa (row 2) and 17 MPa (row 3), computed from the tabulated differences.
No temperature, alloy composition or processing-condition label is printed inside the table; only the measured YS and the two model predictions/differences appear.
The caption states that the table is the 'Experimental verification of model prediction results'.
The citing text states the error reduction was 22 MPa at 750 °C, 21 MPa at 800 °C and 17 MPa at 850 °C, which links the three table rows to those three temperatures.
The citing text states that the contribution values of the various strengthening mechanisms were used as input features and the YS as the output feature for both models.
The citing text frames this table within YS prediction of Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si low-density steel, calculated and measured in Section 4.2.
The citing text concludes that the YS prediction framework based on strengthening-mechanism contributions can be transferred to YS prediction of medium-manganese low-density steel.
The citing text refers to this result together with 'Fig. 15', i.e. the table is read as a companion of a figure not included in this image group.
